name: Jewelry / watch / accessories

angle.text: Style communities use minimal jewelry and watches to finish an outfit and signal taste or status with little effort. The added polish is visible the moment the pieces are worn. Whether accessories change how attractive someone is rated has not been tested in trials.

summary: Understated rings, chains and watches to finish an outfit; rich in history, with no attractiveness trials.
note: Costs range from cheap to luxury; counterfeit luxury watches are common.
currentQuick:
This meta is wearing a few well-chosen accessories, such as a simple watch or ring, to make an outfit look finished.
References document jewellery and watches as long-standing status and identity signals. No study found tests their effect on rated attractiveness.
How it works: Accessories are said to add polish and signal taste or status; the effect depends on context and local norms.
Risks and caveats: Low risk. Reported caveats are cultural norms and a large counterfeit luxury-watch market.
deepLead:
Minimal jewelry, watches and other accessories are used in style communities to polish an outfit and signal taste or status without much effort. Common items include rings, necklaces, bracelets and wristwatches.
No published studies were found on whether accessories change rated attractiveness. Encyclopedic sources document the long history of jewellery as a marker of status and group membership, and of the wristwatch as a military tool that became a fashion and status item.

name: Grooming routine (nails, ear/nose hair)

angle.text: Appearance communities treat tidy nails and trimmed ear and nose hair as basic upkeep that raises perceived polish. The change is visible right after grooming. Its effect on attractiveness ratings has not been studied directly.

summary: Keeping nails and ear and nose hair tidy; basic upkeep with no attractiveness trials.
currentQuick:
This meta is routine upkeep of details such as nails and ear and nose hair, which proponents say raises how polished someone looks.
References place nail trimming within standard hygiene practice. No study found tests these habits for attractiveness.
How it works: Tidy small details are said to signal care and cleanliness to observers.
Risks and caveats: Low risk. Sources reviewed do not describe specific harms.
deepLead:
A grooming routine covering nails and ear and nose hair is a set of basic upkeep habits discussed in appearance communities as raising perceived polish. It sits at the line between hygiene and appearance.
Wikipedia lists trimming fingernails and toenails among generally accepted hygiene practices, and distinguishes grooming such as shaving or combing, which supports a good appearance, from hygiene itself. No published study found tests nail or ear and nose hair care for effects on rated attractiveness.

name: Skin-care baseline routine

chain: Healthier skin barrier, less sun damage
angle.text: Many appearance communities treat cleanser, moisturiser and daily sunscreen as the foundation before any active ingredients or procedures. Users aim for clearer, more even skin and slower visible aging. Sunscreen carries most of the evidence, mainly for photoaging, while the cleanser and moisturiser parts are mostly guidance.

summary: Cleanser, moisturiser and SPF: the dull trio that dermatology guidance treats as the base layer, with sunscreen carrying most of the evidence.
note: Evidence is strongest for sunscreen; little research on cleansers and moisturisers in healthy skin.
currentQuick:
The baseline routine means a gentle cleanser, a moisturiser and a daily broad-spectrum sunscreen. Communities often present it as the foundation for skin quality before anything stronger is added.
Encyclopedic and dermatology sources describe the same basic trio as the generally favoured approach, with other products reserved for particular conditions.
How it works: Cleansers remove oil and residue, moisturisers slow water loss from the skin, and sunscreen filters UV radiation that contributes to sunburn, photoaging and skin cancer.
Risks and caveats: Risks are low. Fragrances or preservatives can cause contact dermatitis, harsh cleansers or over-exfoliation can irritate, and sunscreen protection depends on how much is applied. Paraffin-based moisturisers carry a documented fire risk near flames.
deepLead:
The skin-care baseline routine is the minimal regimen of gentle cleansing, moisturising and daily sun protection that many appearance-focused communities treat as the foundation before any active ingredients, procedures or other interventions are added.
Encyclopedic sources describe a similar basic routine as the one generally favoured in dermatology, with other products reserved for specific conditions such as acne. Sunscreen has the strongest research support of the three steps, with studies reporting reduced sunburn and skin cancer risk and a slowing of photoaging. Wikipedia also notes that there is little scientific knowledge about the clinical benefit of simple habits such as washing and applying lotion, and that anti-aging claims on cosmetic products are generally unproven.

name: Style subreddit / fit-check culture (r/malefashionadvice)

angle.text: Users post outfit photos to communities such as r/malefashionadvice and collect critique from strangers, aiming to refine fit, colour and layering. Changes to clothing choices then show up in how they dress. Whether this feedback loop improves rated attractiveness has not been studied.

summary: Post a fit pic, get strangers' feedback: a free outfit-critique loop with no research on whether it moves the needle.
note: Feedback quality varies by who responds; no studies on effect.
currentQuick:
Fit-check culture means posting your outfit online for feedback. The best known venue is r/malefashionadvice, a Reddit community founded in 2009 with millions of members.
Members use it for outfit critique, shopping questions and identifying garments.
How it works: Users post photos in recurring outfit threads and other members comment on fit, colour and styling. The idea is crowd feedback in place of a personal stylist.
Risks and caveats: Risks are minimal and mostly about privacy when posting photos and uneven advice quality. The community's moderation was disrupted in the 2023 Reddit API protest.
deepLead:
Style subreddit fit-check culture is the practice of posting photographs of one's outfit to an online community and asking for feedback. The best-known example is r/malefashionadvice, a Reddit community where men share outfits and ask for style advice.
According to Wikipedia, the subreddit was founded in September 2009 by Jeremy Wagner-Kaiser, who said he wanted to give plain answers to people who know little about clothing. It reported about 6.3 million users as of August 2025. In appearance-improvement communities it is often cited as a free route to outfit feedback, though no studies have assessed whether such feedback changes how others perceive the person posting.

name: Style AI apps / virtual try-on

angle.text: Appearance communities use virtual try-on and style AI apps to preview clothing, accessories or hairstyles on their own photo before committing. The preview helps narrow choices, and the outfit or look chosen is what changes appearance. How closely previews match real results has not been measured.

summary: Apps that preview outfits or looks on your own photo; handy for browsing, with no evidence on how well previews match reality.
note: Camera and face-photo uploads raise privacy questions; accuracy is not independently evaluated.
currentQuick:
Style AI apps and virtual try-on tools overlay clothes or looks on a photo or live camera view of you. Some also suggest outfits automatically.
People use them to preview a style before buying or committing.
How it works: They combine camera input, body or face measurements and 3D or image-based rendering, with augmented reality tracking the user's movement in live video.
Risks and caveats: Documented limits include fixed-distance requirements, self-measurement errors and lighting sensitivity. Uploading face or body images raises privacy concerns, and no independent accuracy data were found.
deepLead:
Style AI apps and virtual try-on tools are software that let a user preview clothing, accessories or hairstyles on a photo, video feed or avatar of themselves, and in some cases suggest outfits or looks automatically. Appearance communities discuss them as a way to test a style before buying or committing to it.
Encyclopedic coverage of the broader category, virtual dressing rooms, describes size-recommendation systems, body scanners, 3D avatars and augmented-reality overlays that track the user on a camera feed. The article gives no accuracy metrics or independent evaluations, and does not discuss artificial-intelligence methods explicitly. Evidence on how well AI style apps predict real-world appearance or satisfaction is limited.

name: Hairstyle simulators / AI haircut preview

chain: Pick a style that suits face
angle.text: Users upload a selfie to hairstyle simulators to see a haircut on their own face before visiting a stylist, aiming to choose a cut that suits their face shape. The haircut itself is what changes appearance. How closely previews match actual results has not been studied.

summary: Preview a haircut on your own selfie before committing; useful for ideas, with no data on how closely previews match results.
note: Previews ignore hair texture and density; face photos uploaded to apps raise privacy questions.
currentQuick:
Hairstyle simulators place a chosen cut or colour on a photo of your face. AI versions generate the style rather than overlaying a template.
People use them to preview options before visiting a barber or stylist.
How it works: The app detects the face and head in a photo, then renders a hairstyle onto it. Face shape, hair type and head shape are factors the reference sources say affect real-world results.
Risks and caveats: Risks are low. Previews may not reflect hair texture or growth patterns, and uploading face photos raises privacy concerns. No studies test preview accuracy.
deepLead:
Hairstyle simulators, including AI haircut preview tools, are apps and websites that overlay or generate a hairstyle on a user's photo so they can see a cut on their own face before visiting a stylist.
Reference sources say little about the tools themselves. Wikipedia's hairstyle article notes that aesthetic choices may depend on physical attributes such as hair type and face and head shape, alongside desired self-image and the stylist's judgment, but that section is flagged as uncited and gives no guidance on how to match a style to a face. No published study has tested whether previews predict real results.

name: Testosterone gel (AndroGel)

angle.text: Testosterone gel is prescribed for diagnosed low testosterone, and forum users discuss it as a TRT option for muscle, body composition and energy. Trials in hypogonadal men show gains in lean mass and drops in fat mass; use for cosmetic purposes in men with normal levels is off-label and less studied.

summary: Prescription skin-applied testosterone for diagnosed low T; well studied in hypogonadal men, not a cosmetic product.
note: Controlled, prescription-only; can transfer to women and children through skin contact; may raise blood pressure and hematocrit.
currentQuick:
Testosterone gel is a prescription gel applied to the skin to treat low testosterone in men. AndroGel is the best-known brand.
Studies in hypogonadal men report normalised testosterone and improvements in sexual function, mood, lean mass and bone density. Its appearance interest comes from muscle and body composition effects.
How it works: Testosterone is absorbed through the skin into the bloodstream, raising circulating testosterone, with some conversion to dihydrotestosterone and estradiol.
Risks and caveats: Reported effects include acne, breast enlargement, raised hematocrit, sperm suppression and, with other testosterone forms, cardiovascular and clot concerns. Virilisation can occur in exposed women and children. It is a controlled substance requiring a prescription in most countries.
deepLead:
Testosterone gel is a prescription topical form of testosterone replacement therapy applied to the skin, sold under brand names including AndroGel, Testim, TestoGel and Fortesta. It is prescribed mainly for male hypogonadism, in which the body produces too little testosterone, and is also used in masculinising hormone therapy for transgender men.
In a 2004 study of 163 hypogonadal men followed for up to 42 months, continuous gel use normalised average serum testosterone levels. In muscle and appearance-focused communities the gel is discussed as a steadier alternative to injections, usually in the context of testosterone replacement therapy rather than as a cosmetic product. Wikipedia notes that the US FDA stated in 2015 that benefits and safety of testosterone for age-related low testosterone had not been established.

name: Nasal testosterone (Natesto)

angle.text: Natesto is a prescription nasal testosterone for diagnosed low T, discussed in TRT circles mainly because small studies suggest it may keep sperm production and gonadotropins more intact. The appearance link people draw is the usual TRT one, more muscle and less fat, studied in hypogonadal men rather than for cosmetic use.

summary: Prescription testosterone nasal gel for diagnosed low T; small studies suggest it may keep sperm and gonadotropins intact, but not a cosmetic product.
note: Controlled, prescription-only; hematocrit and blood pressure monitoring studies exist; evidence is for hypogonadal men, not appearance.
currentQuick:
Natesto is a prescription testosterone gel given through the nose for men with low testosterone. It is short-acting and aimed at people who want an alternative to skin gels or injections.
Trials in hypogonadal men report normalised testosterone, and several small studies report preserved semen parameters.
How it works: Testosterone absorbed across the nasal lining enters the bloodstream and raises circulating levels for a short period, so it is taken several times a day under a prescriber's direction.
Risks and caveats: As with other testosterone products, reported concerns include raised hematocrit, blood pressure monitoring, acne, and prostate and cardiovascular questions. It is a controlled prescription drug and is banned in competitive sport.
deepLead:
Natesto is a prescription testosterone nasal gel used for testosterone replacement in men with hypogonadism. Wikipedia lists it as the intranasal testosterone product, supplied as a metered spray.
In a 90-day randomised, open-label, dose-ranging study of 306 hypogonadal men, the nasal gel normalised androgen levels, with extensions to one year. It is discussed in muscle and hormone communities mainly as a short-acting option that, in several small studies, did not suppress gonadotropins or sperm in the way other testosterone forms can.

name: Oral testosterone undecanoate (Jatenzo / Kyzatrex)

angle.text: Oral testosterone undecanoate is a prescription capsule form of TRT for diagnosed deficiency, discussed by users as an alternative to injections or gels. The appearance link is the usual TRT one, more lean mass and less fat, studied in men with low testosterone rather than as a looksmaxxing tool.

summary: Prescription capsules that deliver testosterone by mouth for diagnosed deficiency; a medical TRT option, not a studied looksmaxxing tool.
note: US labels for oral testosterone undecanoate products carry blood pressure warnings; prescription-only controlled substance.
currentQuick:
Oral testosterone undecanoate is a prescription capsule form of testosterone replacement therapy. Jatenzo was approved by the US FDA in 2019 as the first oral version, followed by Tlando and Kyzatrex in 2022. It is approved for adult men with low or absent testosterone from specific medical causes.
In looksmaxxing and muscle-focused communities it is discussed mainly as a needle-free alternative to injectable or gel TRT. No published trials examine it for appearance or muscle-building in healthy men.
How it works: Testosterone undecanoate is a prodrug of testosterone. Ordinary oral testosterone is largely cleared by the liver, so these capsules use a lipid-based formulation intended to carry the compound through the lymphatic system and avoid this first-pass loss. Absorption is reported to rise with fatty food and to vary between individuals.
Risks and caveats: Reported effects include raised blood pressure, acne, hair growth, raised liver enzymes and lipid changes. It is a Schedule III controlled substance in the US and requires a prescription. Testosterone products in general can suppress sperm production.
deepLead:
Oral testosterone undecanoate is a testosterone replacement therapy taken by mouth as a capsule. Testosterone undecanoate is a prodrug of testosterone, meaning it is converted to the active hormone in the body . Brand names include Jatenzo, Kyzatrex and Tlando in the United States, and Andriol elsewhere .
The US Food and Drug Administration approved Jatenzo in March 2019 as the first oral testosterone undecanoate product, with Tlando approved in March 2022 and Kyzatrex in July 2022 . These products are indicated for adult men with testosterone deficiency from defined medical conditions rather than for age-related decline or cosmetic purposes .
Within appearance and muscle-oriented communities, oral TRT is discussed as an alternative to injections or gels. No published trials have tested it in healthy men for physique or facial appearance outcomes. The only registered trial in the available record is an early-phase study in menopausal women with low sexual desire .

name: Testosterone pellets (Testopel)

angle.text: Testosterone pellets are implants placed under the skin that release hormone for months, used by people on TRT who prefer fewer doses. The appearance link people draw is more muscle and less fat from restored testosterone, supported by observational data and small trials in men with deficiency.

summary: Rice-grain testosterone implants placed under the skin for months-long TRT; an established medical option with observational and small-trial data.
note: Requires a minor in-office procedure; compounded pellets are not FDA-approved products.
currentQuick:
Testosterone pellets are small solid implants placed under the skin that release testosterone gradually. Testopel is the FDA-approved brand; the US approved implantable pellets in 1972 for testosterone deficiency, and they returned to wider clinical use in recent years.
They appeal to people who want to avoid frequent injections or daily gels. Published work consists mainly of observational studies and a few small trials, not long-term outcome trials.
How it works: Pellets are inserted subcutaneously, typically in the hip or buttock area, and slowly dissolve, releasing testosterone into the bloodstream over several months. Medication overviews list dosing every 3 to 6 months, with pellets in 50, 75, 100 and 200 mg strengths.
Risks and caveats: Because the pellets are implanted, a minor procedure is needed, and reported complications of implant procedures include infection and pellet extrusion. As with other testosterone therapy, effects include acne, raised red blood cell counts, sperm suppression and other systemic effects. Compounded pellets are not the same as the branded FDA-approved product.
deepLead:
Testosterone pellets are small cylindrical implants of crystalline testosterone placed under the skin to provide sustained hormone release. Testopel is the branded product; a 2012 multi-institution study notes that the FDA approved implantable testosterone pellets in 1972 for testosterone deficiency syndrome, and that clinical use was limited until Testopel was reintroduced .
Medication references list pellet doses of 150 to 1,200 mg every 3 to 6 months for men, in strengths of 50 to 200 mg per pellet . Pellets are one of several delivery options alongside injections, gels and oral products .
Evidence consists of observational serum-level studies, patient-preference surveys and small randomised trials, mostly in men with diagnosed hypogonadism . No published trials have examined pellets for appearance outcomes in healthy people.

name: Testosterone undecanoate injection (Aveed)

angle.text: Aveed is a long-acting clinic-administered testosterone injection given every few months for diagnosed deficiency, appealing to people who want infrequent dosing. The appearance link is the usual TRT one, more lean mass and less fat, studied in men with low testosterone rather than for cosmetic goals.

summary: Long-acting testosterone depot injection given in a clinic every few months; approved for deficiency, with a REMS programme for lung oil-embolism and anaphylaxis risk.
note: US product requires a REMS because of pulmonary oil microembolism and anaphylaxis risk.
currentQuick:
Testosterone undecanoate injection is a long-acting testosterone depot sold as Aveed in the US and Nebido in Europe. It is given intramuscularly in a medical setting and is approved for men with testosterone deficiency.
It is discussed in muscle and TRT communities as a way to avoid frequent self-injection. Published studies are in hypogonadal men; no trials examine it for appearance in healthy people.
How it works: The undecanoate ester is dissolved in oil and releases slowly from the muscle depot, where it is converted to testosterone. Intramuscular half-life is reported around 21 days in tea seed oil and 34 days in castor oil.
Risks and caveats: The FDA rejected Aveed three times (2008, 2009 and 2013) over concerns about pulmonary oil microembolism (POME) and anaphylaxis before approving it in 2014 with a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy. Other reported effects are acne, hypertension, raised liver enzymes and lipid changes. It is a Schedule III controlled substance in the US.
deepLead:
Testosterone undecanoate injection is a long-acting intramuscular testosterone preparation marketed as Aveed in the United States and Nebido in Europe . It is a prodrug of testosterone used for replacement therapy in adult men with low or absent endogenous testosterone .
The FDA rejected Aveed in 2008, 2009 and 2013 over pulmonary oil microembolism and anaphylaxis concerns, then approved it in March 2014 with a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy . Nebido received initial European approval in Finland in November 2003 .
Registered studies cover long-term safety in hypogonadal men, blood pressure effects, erectile dysfunction, delayed puberty and others . No studies have examined it for cosmetic outcomes.

name: Sustanon (testosterone blend)

angle.text: Sustanon is a blended testosterone ester injection discussed in bodybuilding circles as a way to build muscle and size. Testosterone's effects on lean mass are well documented in general; this specific blend has no appearance trials of its own.

summary: A blend of four testosterone esters in oil, marketed as Sustanon 250; discussed in bodybuilding circles, with no appearance trials behind it.
note: Prescription testosterone product; sources for this entry are thin.
currentQuick:
Sustanon is the brand name of mixed-ester testosterone injections. Sustanon 250 combines four testosterone esters (propionate, phenylpropionate, isocaproate and decanoate), and Sustanon 100 combines three of them (propionate, phenylpropionate and isocaproate).
The blend is intended to give a mix of faster and slower release. Little published research is available in the sources reviewed for this wiki, and none examines appearance outcomes.
How it works: Each ester is a prodrug that is cleaved to release testosterone after intramuscular injection; shorter esters act sooner and longer ones last longer, so a blend spreads release over time.
Risks and caveats: As with other testosterone products, general risks include acne, sperm suppression, raised red blood cell counts and cardiovascular and prostate considerations. Testosterone is a controlled substance in many countries.
deepLead:
Sustanon is the brand name for blended testosterone ester injectables. Sustanon 250 contains four esters (propionate, phenylpropionate, isocaproate and decanoate), while Sustanon 100 contains three (propionate, phenylpropionate and isocaproate) .
Testosterone esters generally are prodrugs that are converted to testosterone in the body, and injection of esters in oil is the most common route for testosterone replacement . The sources available for this entry do not detail Sustanon's manufacturer history or trial data, so this article is brief.

name: Cabergoline

angle.text: Cabergoline is a prescription prolactin-lowering drug, studied for prolactinomas, and forum users discuss it as an add-on to testosterone or other hormone regimens to manage prolactin side effects. Its link to appearance is indirect and based on anecdote, not on appearance trials.

summary: A prescription dopamine agonist that lowers prolactin; well studied for prolactinomas, discussed online as an add-on to hormone regimens, with documented heart-valve concerns at high doses.
note: Prescription-only; ergot-derived drugs have been linked to cardiac valve disease and fibrosis, mainly at the higher doses used in Parkinson's disease.
currentQuick:
Cabergoline is an ergot-derived, long-acting dopamine D2 receptor agonist taken by mouth. Its US-labelled use is for hyperprolactinemic disorders, including those caused by pituitary adenomas, and it is generally preferred over bromocriptine for prolactinomas.
In muscle and TRT-oriented communities it is discussed as a way to manage prolactin during hormone therapy. Published trials are in prolactinomas and other pituitary conditions, not in healthy people seeking appearance changes.
How it works: It stimulates D2 receptors on prolactin-producing pituitary cells, mimicking dopamine's inhibitory signal and lowering prolactin secretion; in prolactinomas it also shrinks tumours. Its half-life is long, reported around 63 to 115 hours depending on the population.
Risks and caveats: Common effects are nausea, headache, dizziness and constipation. Ergot-derived dopamine agonists have been associated with cardiac valve regurgitation, mainly at high Parkinson's-disease doses, and the label advises cardiovascular evaluation including echocardiography. Rare pulmonary and other fibrotic complications are reported. It is prescription-only.
deepLead:
Cabergoline is an ergoline-derived dopamine D2 receptor agonist taken orally, sold under brand names such as Dostinex and Cabaser . The US drug label lists its indication as hyperprolactinemic disorders, either idiopathic or due to pituitary adenomas .
For prolactinomas, a 2017 JAMA review states that initial therapy is generally a dopamine agonist . A 1994 double-blind trial of 459 women with hyperprolactinemic amenorrhea compared cabergoline with bromocriptine . Wikipedia reports that the drug was synthesised by Farmitalia-Carlo Erba in Milan, marketed in the Netherlands in 1992 and approved by the FDA in December 1996 .
Safety debates centre on cardiac valve disease. Two 2007 studies in Parkinson's disease patients found associations between pergolide and cabergoline and valve regurgitation . Cabergoline has also been studied in ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome, acromegaly and Cushing's disease . No published trials have examined it for appearance outcomes.

name: FSH / Menopur (HMG)

angle.text: FSH and Menopur come from IVF medicine and are discussed in TRT circles as a way to keep sperm production and testicular function going alongside testosterone. The appearance link is only that of sustaining a TRT regimen's muscle and body-composition goals; the evidence base is in fertility treatment, not looks.

summary: Fertility gonadotropins (FSH, hMG) from IVF medicine, discussed in TRT circles as a way to keep sperm production going; the evidence is in women's fertility, not appearance.
note: Prescription fertility drugs with monitoring requirements; trial evidence is mostly in women undergoing IVF.
currentQuick:
Menopur is a brand of highly purified menotropin (human menopausal gonadotropin, hMG), a mixture of FSH and LH activity originally extracted from the urine of postmenopausal women. It is used to stimulate the ovaries in fertility treatment, and the same drug class can be used in hypogonadal men to stimulate sperm production.
In looksmaxxing and TRT communities these gonadotropins come up as fertility-preserving companions to testosterone therapy. The published trials are almost all in women having IVF, and none examine appearance outcomes.
How it works: FSH acts on ovarian follicles in women and on Sertoli cells in men to support gamete production, while LH activity stimulates sex-hormone production. Menopur supplies both activities; recombinant FSH products supply FSH alone.
Risks and caveats: Known concerns in women's fertility treatment include ovarian overstimulation and multiple pregnancy. These are prescription drugs given by injection under monitoring. Specific harms in men using them alongside testosterone are not covered by the trials listed here.
deepLead:
Menotropin, also called human menopausal gonadotropin (hMG), is a fertility drug extracted from the urine of postmenopausal women, whose urine is rich in FSH and LH . Menopur, made by Ferring, is a highly purified preparation; earlier products included Pergonal .
The extraction method was developed by Piero Donini in 1949 and brought into clinical use by Bruno Lunenfeld in 1961 . Wikipedia notes recombinant FSH has largely replaced hMG in many settings and that a Cochrane analysis found no major clinical outcome differences between urinary and recombinant FSH .
Trial evidence is concentrated in women undergoing IVF or ovulation induction . The 'FSH' entry in this wiki reflects use of gonadotropins in men on testosterone therapy, a use for which the sources reviewed contain no trial data on appearance outcomes.

name: Fenugreek

angle.text: Fenugreek seed extract is sold as a natural testosterone and libido supplement, taken by lifters hoping for better training results and body composition. Small trials of branded extracts report modest hormone changes, while evidence for visible muscle or physique change is limited.

summary: A culinary seed sold as an herbal testosterone and libido supplement; small trials of branded extracts report modest hormone changes, but evidence is limited.
note: Not considered safe in pregnancy; may lower blood sugar and interact with anticoagulant and diabetes drugs.
currentQuick:
Fenugreek is a Mediterranean and South Asian plant whose seeds are used as a spice and in traditional medicine. In looksmaxxing and fitness circles it is sold as a natural testosterone booster, usually as seed extract capsules.
A few small randomized trials of specific extracts, and meta-analyses of them, report increases in total testosterone or sexual-function scores in some men. Reviewers describe the evidence as limited by few studies, varied extracts and small samples.
How it works: Proponents attribute effects to steroidal saponins (such as protodioscin) and other seed compounds. Proposed mechanisms in the research literature include effects on androgen and estrogen pathways, though human mechanistic data are limited.
Risks and caveats: Reported side effects include diarrhea, bloating and gas, and a maple-like body odor. Wikipedia notes it may lower blood sugar and interfere with anticoagulants, and that it is not considered safe in pregnancy. It is sold as a dietary supplement in the US, not an approved drug.
deepLead:
Fenugreek (Trigonella foenum-graecum) is an annual legume native to the Near East and Mediterranean whose seeds and leaves are widely used as a spice and herb, particularly in South Asian cooking . It has a long history in traditional medicine, including documented use in ancient Egypt and Greek and Indian medicine .
In appearance-focused and fitness communities, fenugreek seed extract is discussed as an herbal "testosterone booster" and libido aid, and is a common ingredient in multi-herb men's-health products .
Several small randomized trials of specific extracts, and meta-analyses pooling them, have reported higher total testosterone or improved sexual-function scores in some men; systematic reviews describe these findings as limited by few trials, differing extracts and small samples . Wikipedia states that no high-quality evidence supports therapeutic properties and that the US FDA has not approved fenugreek for clinical use .

name: D-aspartic acid (DAA)

chain: Amino acid marketed to raise testosterone
angle.text: D-aspartic acid is sold as a testosterone booster for men who lift. Early work suggested a hormonal role, but trials in trained men found no testosterone increase and, at higher intake, a decrease, so the muscle-building claim is untested beyond that.

summary: An amino acid sold as a testosterone booster; early work suggested a hormonal role, but trials in trained men found no increase and, at higher intake, a decrease.
note: Three randomized trials in resistance-trained men reported no testosterone increase; one reported lower testosterone at the higher intake tested.
currentQuick:
D-aspartic acid is the mirror-image (D-form) of the common amino acid aspartic acid, found naturally in the pituitary gland and testes. It is sold as a sports supplement marketed for raising testosterone.
A 2009 study reported that sodium D-aspartate increased luteinizing hormone and testosterone in humans and rats. Later randomized trials in resistance-trained men found no testosterone rise, and one found lower testosterone at 6 grams per day.
How it works: Laboratory work in rats proposes that D-aspartate acts in the pituitary to increase LH release and in testicular Leydig cells to raise testosterone synthesis, via cGMP and cAMP signaling. Human trials in trained men did not show this effect.
Risks and caveats: The trials report no major safety signals, but one reported lower total and free testosterone with 6 g/day, and another reported a 16 percent drop in estradiol. It is sold as a dietary supplement; long-term safety data are limited.
deepLead:
D-aspartic acid (DAA) is the D-enantiomer of aspartic acid, one of two D-amino acids commonly found in mammals; it is largely not used to build proteins and is found in tissues including the pituitary gland and testes . It is sold as a dietary supplement marketed for raising testosterone, particularly to men who lift weights.
The marketing rests on a 2009 report that sodium D-aspartate raised luteinizing hormone (LH) and testosterone in humans and rats . Subsequent randomized, placebo-controlled trials in resistance-trained men published between 2013 and 2017 found no increase in testosterone, and one found lower testosterone at the higher intake tested .

name: Horny goat weed (Epimedium)

chain: Icariin acts on PDE5 in the lab
angle.text: Horny goat weed is a Chinese herb sold for libido, erections and vigour, and lists in testosterone-support stacks. Its appearance link is a loose belief about male vitality and hormones. Icariin shows activity in the lab, but human trial evidence is minimal.

summary: A Chinese medicinal herb sold as a libido and erection supplement; its flavonoid icariin inhibits PDE5 in the lab, but human trial evidence is minimal.
note: Evidence for sexual benefit comes mainly from animal and in vitro work; no published human trial on libido was found.
currentQuick:
Horny goat weed refers to plants of the genus Epimedium, used for centuries in traditional Chinese medicine as a kidney and yang tonic. The supplement form is typically E. grandiflorum or extracts standardized to icariin, sold for libido and erectile function.
Icariin is a weak PDE5 inhibitor in vitro, and animal studies report improved erectile function. Wikipedia states there is little clinical evidence to date, and a recent review says clinical efficacy still needs confirmation in randomized trials.
How it works: In animal and cell studies icariin has been reported to act through nitric oxide/cGMP signaling, Rho kinase inhibition and weak PDE5 inhibition, the same enzyme targeted by sildenafil and tadalafil, though at far lower potency.
Risks and caveats: Human safety data are limited. It is sold as a dietary supplement; a US homeopathic-labelled testosterone-support product listing it advises consulting a physician if pregnant or breastfeeding. Interaction data with PDE5 inhibitor drugs are not established in the sources reviewed.
deepLead:
Horny goat weed is the common English name for plants of the genus Epimedium (family Berberidaceae), most of which are native to China . The Chinese name yin yang huo is rendered literally as lascivious goat herb . Traditional Chinese medicine has used it as a tonic for kidney yang deficiency, including low libido and fatigue .
Its supposed aphrodisiac activity is attributed to icariin, a prenylated flavonoid that has been described as a weak PDE5 inhibitor in vitro . Wikipedia states clinical effects are unknown and there is little clinical evidence to date . Reviews of icariin describe erectogenic effects in animal models and say clinical confirmation in high-quality trials is still needed .

name: Maca root

angle.text: Maca is an Andean root sold as a libido and energy supplement and included in testosterone-support stacks. Its appearance link is a general male-vitality belief rather than a visible change. A small number of trials suggest a possible benefit for sexual desire; effects on testosterone or physique are less supported.

summary: An Andean root vegetable sold as a libido and energy supplement; a small number of trials suggest possible benefit for sexual desire, with limited evidence overall.
note: A systematic review described evidence as limited; a French agency warned about possible health risks of powdered root, which others dispute.
currentQuick:
Maca is a radish-like root grown at high altitude in the Peruvian Andes, eaten as food for centuries and now sold worldwide as powder, capsules and extracts. It is marketed for libido, energy and fertility.
A 2010 systematic review found four randomized trials, with two reporting improved sexual desire or function, one reporting an effect in men with erectile dysfunction and one finding no effect in cyclists; its authors called the evidence limited. A 2026 review reports improved libido in men-only and mixed-sex studies and inconsistent results in women.
How it works: The mechanism is not established. Maca does not appear to contain hormones; proposed actives include glucosinolates, macamides and alkaloids such as imidazoles, and Wikipedia notes that no pharmacokinetic data have been published.
Risks and caveats: Maca has a long record as food in the Andes. Wikipedia notes extracts contain MTCA, a compound that may act as an MAO inhibitor, and that France's food-safety agency warned consumers about powdered root, a concern others dispute on the grounds that boiling deactivates it.
deepLead:
Maca (Lepidium meyenii) is a biennial plant of the cabbage family cultivated at 4,000 to 4,500 meters in the central Andes of Peru, grown for its fleshy hypocotyl-taproot . Archaeological evidence shows cultivation around Lake Junín from about 1700 BC, and Spanish chroniclers described it in the early 1600s . Commercial interest grew from the late 1980s, driven by its purported effect on fertility .
In supplement markets it is sold for libido, stamina and hormonal balance, and is a common ingredient in men's testosterone and sexual-health products . Wikipedia describes research on its medicinal properties as inconclusive . A 2010 systematic review concluded there is limited evidence for its effectiveness on sexual function .

name: Panax ginseng

angle.text: Panax ginseng is a traditional East Asian root sold for energy, libido and testosterone, and used in hormone-support stacks. The appearance link is a loose vitality belief rather than a visible change. A Cochrane review found small effects on erectile function that were likely not clinically meaningful.

summary: A classic East Asian adaptogen root sold for energy, libido and testosterone; a Cochrane review found small, likely not clinically meaningful effects on erectile function.
note: Can interact with drugs such as warfarin; reported side effects include headache, insomnia and raised blood pressure.
currentQuick:
Panax ginseng is a perennial root herb from the Russian Far East, northeast China and Korea, central to traditional East Asian medicine as a tonic. It is processed as white or red ginseng and sold as capsules, extracts and drinks for energy, stress and sexual function.
In men with mild to moderate erectile dysfunction, a Cochrane review of nine placebo-controlled trials (587 men) found small improvements in erectile function that were likely not clinically meaningful, mostly on low-certainty evidence. Wikipedia states there is little evidence of a health effect.
How it works: The active constituents are thought to be ginsenosides, triterpene saponins that have been studied for effects on inflammation, vascular tone and nitric oxide signaling. Network-pharmacology and laboratory work proposes multiple targets; human mechanistic evidence is limited.
Risks and caveats: Wikipedia lists headache, raised blood pressure, diarrhea, insomnia and rash as common side effects, notes possible interactions with prescription drugs such as warfarin, and says use in pregnancy and breastfeeding is potentially unsafe.
deepLead:
Panax ginseng, also called Asian, Chinese or Korean ginseng, is a perennial plant native to mountainous areas of the Russian Far East, northeast China and the Korean peninsula; its root is the original source of ginseng and is harvested after five or six years of cultivation . It is used in folk and traditional medicine as a tonic .
In appearance and fitness communities and the wider supplement market it is sold for energy, stress, libido and testosterone support, and appears in multi-herb men's-health products . Research has examined it for erectile dysfunction, fatigue, cognition and other outcomes. A Cochrane review concluded that effects on erectile function were small and probably not clinically meaningful, with mostly low-certainty evidence . Wikipedia states there is little evidence that it provides any health effect, and that its constituents are under preliminary research .

name: Mucuna pruriens

angle.text: Mucuna pruriens is a bean rich in natural L-DOPA, sold as a dopamine, libido and testosterone supplement and discussed online as a way to dopamine max. Human evidence exists mainly for Parkinson's disease; the appearance and hormone uses rest on small studies and anecdote.

summary: A tropical bean rich in natural L-DOPA, used in Ayurveda and sold as a dopamine, libido and testosterone supplement; human evidence exists mainly for Parkinson's disease.
note: Contains L-DOPA; nausea and vomiting are reported at higher intakes and MAO inhibitor users are advised to avoid it. Pod hairs cause severe itching.
currentQuick:
Mucuna pruriens is a climbing legume whose seeds contain roughly 3 to 6 percent L-DOPA, the precursor to dopamine. Ayurvedic tradition uses the seeds as a nerve tonic and aphrodisiac, and the powder is sold as a supplement for mood, motivation, libido and male fertility.
The human evidence is mainly in Parkinson's disease: a small crossover study of 8 patients found seed powder gave faster onset and longer on-time than standard levodopa/carbidopa. No human trial for appearance-related use was found; fertility and testosterone claims rest on animal studies.
How it works: L-DOPA is converted to dopamine by the enzyme aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase. Forum users discuss pairing it with other supplements to modify this pathway; in Parkinson's treatment, levodopa is combined with a peripheral decarboxylase inhibitor because much converts to dopamine outside the brain.
Risks and caveats: L-DOPA sensitivity can cause nausea, vomiting, cramping, arrhythmias and low blood pressure, according to Wikipedia, which advises people on MAOIs to avoid the plant. A looksmax.org user reported vomiting after taking many capsules. Contact with raw pod hairs causes severe itching.
deepLead:
Mucuna pruriens, the velvet bean, is a tropical climbing legume native to Africa and tropical Asia, grown as forage and green manure and eaten in parts of Indonesia . Its seeds contain about 3 to 6 percent L-DOPA (levodopa), the dopamine precursor used in Parkinson's disease treatment, while its pod hairs contain compounds that cause intense itching .
Traditional Indian and African medicine uses the seeds as an aphrodisiac, nervine tonic and remedy for male infertility and Parkinsonian conditions . In looksmaxxing and biohacking forums it is discussed as a source of dopamine, motivation and libido . A small randomized crossover trial in Parkinson's disease reported that seed powder acted faster and gave longer on-time than standard levodopa/carbidopa . No published human trial of its use for appearance, testosterone or fertility was found among the sources reviewed; related findings come from animal studies .
